## Anomaly
{"kind": "conflict", "system": "shop/pricing", "title": "Prices disagree between shop, pads, HUD and brief", "expected": "One price per upgrade across the shop card, world pad, HUD hint and spec. The brief says Dropper 2 costs 25 and the acceptance check uses 10.", "observed": "Round 1 shop cards show $10, $30, $100, $200, $1500 and $2500, while the HUD says 'Next: Dropper 25' and 'Fast Belt 50'. Buying Silver in the shop dropped cash from 36 to 8 (28 spent) against a $30 label. The round judge also flagged inconsistent Dropper 2 and Speed 1 prices.", "severity": "medium"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "Upgrade prices are not driven by one source. The live ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades module that the server and client actually require has a different cost table from the Upgrades.luau file in the repo. The repo file has 10/60/120/250/500/900/1400/2200/4000/7000. The live module has 10/30/60/100/200/350/500/800/1500/2500, with a different budget comment (ore values 1/3/8/20) to match. The shop cards, pads and server purchase all read u.cost from this live module, so they agree with each other but not with the spec. The HUD hint ('Dropper 25', 'Fast Belt 50') uses a third set of numbers that match neither table. The brief (25) and the acceptance check (10) also disagree. The result is that several price sets coexist for the same upgrades. I did not read JuiceService or Hud, so where the 25/50 values come from is unconfirmed. The 28-vs-30 spend on Silver is probably cash income arriving during the purchase, not a pricing bug.", "file": "ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau", "evidence": "Server probe of require(Upgrades).list returned dropper2:10, tier_silver:30, speed1:60, dropper3:100, mult1:200, tier_gold:350, speed2:500, dropper4:800, mult2:1500, tier_diamond:2500. The repo file reads 10, 60, 120, 250, 500, 900, 1400, 2200, 4000, 7000. The live module source (3824 chars, no children) has a different budget comment, with 2x3x1.0/2=3.0/s for silver where the repo file has 12. The shop cards ($10, $30, $100, $200, $1500, $2500) match the live module, while the HUD show

Probe (Server): Check runtime server-side costs versus the source file (10,60,120,...)
```luau
local U=require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Upgrades) local t={} for _,u in ipairs(U.list) do table.insert(t,u.id..":"..tostring(u.cost)) end return table.concat(t,",")
```
Result: dropper2:10,tier_silver:30,speed1:60,dropper3:100,mult1:200,tier_gold:350,speed2:500,dropper4:800,mult2:1500,tier_diamond:2500

Probe (Server): Find scripts that reference Upgrades and assign cost, to locate the runtime mutation of Upgrades costs (runtime costs differ from the source file)
```luau
local out={} for _,d in ipairs(game:GetDescendants()) do if d:IsA('LuaSourceContainer') then local ok,s=pcall(function() return d.Source end) if ok and s and (s:find('Upgrades') and (s:find('%.cost%s*=') or s:find('cost%s*=%s*%d') or s:find('byId'))) then table.insert(out,d:GetFullName()) end end end return table.concat(out,'\n')
```
Result: StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.ShopUi
StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.UpgradeFx
ReplicatedStorage.Upgrades
ServerScriptService.UpgradeService

Probe (Server): Compare the live module source against the file we read to find where the 30/100/200 costs come from
```luau
local m=game.ReplicatedStorage.Upgrades local s=m.Source local i=s:find('tier_silver') return #s..' | '..s:sub(math.max(1,i-60),i+400)..' | children:'..#m:GetChildren()
```

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```

```luau
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

if not p then error("setup: no player") end

if owns then owns:Destroy() end
cash.Value = oldCash
return { ok = not bought and after == 3 and not owns,
```
